sentence: She draws inspiration from urban landscapes.
rationale: Urban landscapes are a familiar visual setting that gives urban a direct city-related meaning.

sentence: Who of those who have been cast down by sin shall ascend?
rationale: The archaic religious question about being cast down by sin and ascending makes cast depend on a fixed biblical-style idiom rather than a clear default context.

sentence: Capitalism is the problem, but Marxism-Leninism is not the solution.
rationale: Capitalism and Marxism-Leninism are presented as competing political solutions, so solution is embedded in an ideological claim unsuitable for a neutral default example.

sentence: Tom's credit score isn't very good.
rationale: A credit score being low is a common personal-finance context that clearly demonstrates score.

sentence: Tom and Mary took a scenic hike along the coast.
rationale: Taking a scenic hike along the coast is a complete, ordinary activity context for hike.

sentence: We have been speaking against the persistent callous attacks in the country.
rationale: Persistent callous attacks in an unnamed country create a loaded political and violence context that is unnecessary for teaching persistent.

sentence: Read the example config file. All the supported configuration options are documented there.
rationale: A config file with documented configuration options gives configuration a direct technical-documentation meaning.

sentence: The bank's actions seemed to assure investors about the soundness of the governmental bonds.
rationale: A bank's actions assuring investors about bonds gives assure a clear formal confidence-building meaning.

sentence: How do you "cancel" one of the most powerful people on the planet?
rationale: Canceling one of the most powerful people invokes cancel-culture discourse and a public power struggle rather than a neutral use of cancel.

sentence: Grace is found in the heart of the humble.
rationale: Finding grace in the heart of the humble is a short, understandable descriptive use of humble.

sentence: Larry came in from the kitchen, a woebegone expression on his face.
rationale: A woebegone facial expression after coming from the kitchen gives expression a clear visible-emotion meaning.

sentence: Privacy is a fundamental human right.
rationale: Calling privacy a fundamental human right gives fundamental a clear importance-and-basis meaning in a modern civic sentence.

sentence: They probably wouldn't sue us over such a minor mistake, but we might as well double-check the contract.
rationale: Considering a lawsuit over a minor mistake and checking a contract is a clear everyday legal context for sue.

sentence: Am I more at risk if my relatives have cancer?
rationale: Asking about personal cancer risk from relatives is a sensitive medical-genetics question, not a neutral default context for cancer.

sentence: Clouds are the veil behind which the face of day coquettishly hides itself, to enhance its beauty.
rationale: The clouds-as-veil personification is ornate and poetic, so veil is not shown in a straightforward modern context.

sentence: Invariant virtue appears to be as mechanical as uninterrupted vice, for true excellence changes with conditions.
rationale: Invariant virtue and uninterrupted vice form an abstract philosophical argument with no concrete situation to anchor vice.

sentence: This is the right lane to be in.
rationale: Identifying the right lane to be in is a short, direct driving context for lane.

sentence: My dad is the dean of admissions.
rationale: A dean of admissions is a familiar education-administration role that clearly teaches dean.

sentence: I was in denial of being an emo kid.
rationale: Being in denial about being an emo kid gives denial a clear refusal-to-accept meaning in an ordinary self-description.

sentence: The intergalactic alliance was in danger of collapsing.
rationale: An intergalactic alliance is a science-fiction setting, so alliance is not grounded in a normal default-learning context.

sentence: Tom wanted to go out in a blaze of glory.
rationale: Going out in a blaze of glory is a widely understood idiom that clearly demonstrates blaze.

sentence: Further discussion of this topic is unlikely to be beneficial.
rationale: Discussion being unlikely to be beneficial gives beneficial a simple evaluation-of-value meaning.

sentence: I cherish the silence, for it speaks louder than words.
rationale: Cherishing silence is a natural personal-preference sentence that directly demonstrates cherish.

sentence: Europe is devising a strategy to prevent water-borne diseases.
rationale: Europe devising a strategy to prevent water-borne diseases gives strategy a clear plan-for-a-goal meaning.

sentence: You'll get a discount on your next order.
rationale: A discount on a next order is a familiar retail context that makes discount concrete.

sentence: Place a few oysters at one time in a wire frying basket and immerse in smoking hot fat.
rationale: Immersing oysters in a frying basket is a complete cooking instruction that clearly shows immerse as putting something into a liquid or fat.

sentence: The evidence for this is fragmentary and could have other interpretations.
rationale: Fragmentary evidence with possible interpretations gives evidence a clear support-for-a-claim meaning.

sentence: Barges filled with tourists glide around hairpin bends, past cobblestone walkways and beneath arched stone bridges.
rationale: Tourist barges gliding around bends provide a concrete movement scene for glide.

sentence: She studies the symbolism in Renaissance art.
rationale: Studying symbolism in Renaissance art gives Renaissance a clear historical-art context.

sentence: There was only one candidate running for the office unopposed, so I wrote in our cat.
rationale: An unopposed office candidate and a write-in joke still make candidate's election meaning immediately clear.

sentence: In a heat exchanger, the molten salt turns water into steam for turbines that turn electrical generators.
rationale: Electrical generators in a heat-exchanger system provide a precise but understandable engineering context for electrical.

sentence: This store isn't exactly in a prime location.
rationale: A store having a prime location gives prime a familiar best-or-most-desirable meaning.

sentence: I don't think Tom is royalty.
rationale: Saying someone is royalty is a short, direct status description that clearly teaches royalty.

sentence: Abject poverty and lack of work has led people to go to extreme measures.
rationale: Extreme poverty leading to extreme measures shows extreme as unusually severe in a coherent social context.

sentence: But when the test results are broken down by subgroup, the differences are dramatic.
rationale: Differences between test subgroups being dramatic gives dramatic a clear large-or-striking meaning.

sentence: Improved conditions elevate the human experience.
rationale: Improved conditions elevating the human experience gives elevate a clear figurative raise-or-improve meaning.

sentence: Are you confident in the outcome?
rationale: Asking whether someone is confident in an outcome is a natural, self-contained use of confident.

sentence: I can detect that there are other dimensions parallel to this one.
rationale: Detecting other dimensions presents detect as noticing or discovering something, and the sentence keeps that target central.

sentence: It's illegal to aid and abet another person in committing a felony.
rationale: Aid and abet in an illegal felony context gives illegal a clear law-based prohibition meaning.

sentence: What did this company's hardworking employees do to deserve such bosses?
rationale: Questioning what hardworking employees deserve from their bosses gives deserve a clear fairness-and-entitlement meaning.

sentence: Compromise only makes sense when all parties are acting in good faith.
rationale: Compromise depending on good faith gives compromise a direct negotiation meaning in a concise general statement.

sentence: But Mr. Duxbury says that despite its extraordinary lightness, aerogel can be quite sturdy.
rationale: Aerogel's extraordinary lightness provides a concrete comparison that clearly demonstrates extraordinary.

sentence: Every grave in this cemetery is identical. It must be where they bury suburbanites.
rationale: Identical graves and a joke about burying suburbanites make identical depend on morbid humor and add little safe teaching value.

sentence: Researchers wanted to know how color vision affected an animal's ability to find camouflaged prey.
rationale: Color vision affecting an animal's search for camouflaged prey gives vision a clear biological-sensory meaning.

sentence: There were no galaxies or even stars, only diffuse gas.
rationale: Diffuse gas filling space without stars is a concrete astronomy context that clearly shows diffuse.

sentence: Tom and Mary booked a flight to an exotic destination.
rationale: An exotic destination is vague travel-marketing language with no concrete referent, so exotic is not taught precisely.

sentence: If you lift that candlestick, it'll move the bookcase and grant us access to the cellar.
rationale: A hidden bookcase granting access to a cellar gives cellar a concrete household-space meaning despite the playful mystery setup.

sentence: Floating in zero gravity is a unique experience for astronauts.
rationale: Floating in zero gravity as a unique astronaut experience gives unique a clear one-of-a-kind meaning.

sentence: She has a masculine way of talking.
rationale: Describing a woman's way of talking as masculine relies on a gender stereotype rather than a neutral, broadly useful context for masculine.

sentence: There are added political risks to quantitative easing in the eurozone, said Brooks.
rationale: Quantitative easing, eurozone risks, and a named speaker create dense policy-finance background that overwhelms quantitative.

sentence: A dog is that animal which another dog will instinctively recognize as such.
rationale: A dog instinctively recognizing another dog gives recognize a clear perception-and-identification meaning.

sentence: A common side effect of amphetamines is severe diarrhea of the mouth.
rationale: Severe diarrhea of the mouth is a vulgar body-based insult, not a reliable natural or useful default context for severe.

sentence: Nuts may be purchased shelled or unshelled with the exception of cashews, which are sold only shelled.
rationale: Cashews being the exception to the shelled-or-unshelled purchase rule gives exception a clear exclusion meaning.

sentence: Tom bought a snack from the vending machine.
rationale: Buying a snack from a vending machine is a simple everyday purchase context for snack.

sentence: Some birds migrate to roost during specific seasons.
rationale: Birds migrating to roost during seasons gives migrate a clear recurring movement meaning.

sentence: The Danish glottal stop is just the speaker's vocal cords giving up briefly in protest.
rationale: A Danish glottal stop and vocal-cord terminology require specialist phonetics knowledge that overwhelms vocal.

sentence: China has no right to impose its rule on the people of Taiwan.
rationale: China imposing rule on Taiwan is a charged geopolitical claim, so impose is not shown in a neutral default context.

sentence: You don't know me or what I'm capable of.
rationale: You don't know me or what I'm capable of is an incomplete challenge with no action or ability specified, so capable is poorly anchored.

sentence: If I go back to their disastrous recipes, may the devil take me.
rationale: Disastrous recipes paired with may the devil take me is an odd archaic curse, so disastrous is not taught through a useful natural context.

sentence: Can you read the rough draft of my essay?
rationale: Asking someone to read an essay's rough draft gives draft a clear writing-stage meaning.

sentence: The musician releases her less successful works into the public domain.
rationale: Releasing less successful music into the public domain gives domain a clear legal-ownership context.

sentence: I think I'm on the ace spectrum.
rationale: Describing oneself as on the ace spectrum is a concise, neutral identity use that clearly shows spectrum as a range.

sentence: A clerk at the feed store convinced him to try raising a cow.
rationale: A clerk at a feed store is a concrete retail role in a complete everyday sentence.

sentence: Have you ever hated someone for being gorgeous?
rationale: Asking whether someone has hated a person for being gorgeous gives gorgeous a clear appearance meaning.

sentence: They should fully fund missile defense programs.
rationale: Funding missile-defense programs places fund inside a militarized policy debate rather than a neutral money-support context.

sentence: Tinfoil hats actually amplify the mind control signals. That's how they get you.
rationale: Tinfoil hats amplifying mind-control signals is a conspiracy claim, so amplify is not presented in a reliable modern learning context.

sentence: Rachel's going to be out of commission for a while.
rationale: Being out of commission is a common idiom for being unable to work or function, clearly teaching commission.

sentence: The ultraviolet light disinfects wastewater so completely that bacteria and other harmful microorganisms cannot grow.
rationale: Ultraviolet light disinfecting wastewater gives ultraviolet a concrete scientific-property context.

sentence: The island was a paradise with white sandy beaches.
rationale: An island with white sandy beaches being paradise is a familiar, concrete ideal-place description.

sentence: Tom's knowledge of decomposition ecology is peerless.
rationale: Decomposition ecology is a specialist scientific compound that provides too much background and does not teach ecology in an accessible way.

sentence: What are the most effective ways to manage a crisis?
rationale: Asking for effective ways to manage a crisis is a clear practical problem-solving context.

sentence: Do we need more oxygen tanks?
rationale: Asking whether more oxygen tanks are needed gives oxygen a concrete medical-equipment context without offering unsafe advice.

sentence: I seek calm in the midst of chaos.
rationale: Seeking calm in the midst of chaos is a common contrast that directly demonstrates midst.

sentence: It's not that your criticism is too controversial, but that it's facile.
rationale: Calling criticism facile while discussing whether it is controversial gives controversial a clear disputed-or-sensitive meaning.

sentence: The facsimile proved that the inscription was genuine.
rationale: A facsimile proving an inscription genuine gives genuine a clear authentic-not-fake meaning.

sentence: Do your best, and that will suffice.
rationale: Doing one's best being sufficient is a familiar, self-contained use of suffice.

sentence: The ballroom was filled with the scent of roses.
rationale: A ballroom filled with the scent of roses is a concrete sensory setting for scent.

sentence: Do you know anything about the history or origin of this flag?
rationale: Asking about a flag's history or origin gives origin a direct beginning-or-source meaning.

sentence: The decision of the jury in the Depp-Heard case was legally baseless.
rationale: The Depp-Heard case is a highly charged public legal dispute and the sentence asks the learner to evaluate a verdict, not simply learn jury.

sentence: Radiation and convection carry that energy outward to the star's surface and to its atmosphere beyond.
rationale: Radiation and convection carrying energy outward gives outward a precise directional meaning in an understandable science context.

sentence: That's not much of an incentive.
rationale: That's not much of an incentive supplies no goal or motivating factor, so incentive is left as an unexplained abstract label.

sentence: To stand tall is to be vulnerable.
rationale: To stand tall is to be vulnerable is a paradoxical aphorism without a concrete situation, so vulnerable is not taught clearly enough.

sentence: On the slope of the roof two men were repairing the tiling.
rationale: Repairing roof tiles on a slope gives slope a concrete surface-and-position meaning.

sentence: Wasps help keep insect populations down.
rationale: Wasps reducing insect populations gives insect a clear biological group meaning.

sentence: Tom is going to teach me to tame dragons.
rationale: Teaching someone to tame dragons is a fantasy premise and does not provide a normal default-learning context for tame.

sentence: Tom must be turning over in his grave.
rationale: Turning over in one's grave is a widely understood idiom that gives grave a clear burial-place meaning.

sentence: It was a mistake to amplify this debate with thoughtless responses.
rationale: Amplifying a debate with thoughtless responses gives debate a clear public-discussion meaning.

sentence: Do you promote hygiene at work?
rationale: Promoting hygiene at work is a direct workplace-health use that clearly demonstrates promote.

sentence: Nasa's aerogels are made from a special silica glass gel that's been mixed to the consistency of pudding.
rationale: Aerogel mixed to the consistency of pudding gives pudding a concrete texture comparison.

sentence: He sees opportunity in every setback.
rationale: Seeing opportunity in every setback is a common resilience context that clearly shows setback.

sentence: Through those two days the train seemed to meander in a leisurely fashion through varied and attractive country.
rationale: Attractive country along a leisurely train journey gives attractive a clear visual-appeal meaning.

sentence: I am living proof that you failed to break me.
rationale: Living proof that someone failed to break the speaker gives proof a clear evidence meaning.

sentence: Regardless of your personal misogynistic hatred of the defendant, she did not break any laws.
rationale: Misogynistic hatred of a defendant introduces explicit gendered hostility into a legal dispute, making hatred a severe unsuitable context.

sentence: A slab of concrete underlies nearly every permanent structure on Earth.
rationale: A permanent structure made of concrete gives permanent a clear lasting-duration meaning.

sentence: There's a famous case of a jackdaw nest in India that was composed entirely of gold spectacle frames.
rationale: Gold spectacle frames in a jackdaw nest give spectacle a concrete eyeglasses-related meaning.

sentence: Sour cream and onion is my favorite potato chip flavor.
rationale: Sour cream and onion chips provide a familiar food-flavor context for sour.

sentence: Provided that one day I have a place to plant olive trees!
rationale: The conditional fragment about someday planting olive trees has no complete proposition, so olive is not presented in a reliable standalone sentence.

sentence: Did they vote for freedom and equality?
rationale: Voting for freedom and equality gives equality a clear civic fairness meaning in a short sentence.

sentence: You can't prohibit me from doing that.
rationale: You can't prohibit me from doing that is a direct, ordinary use of prohibit as forbid.

sentence: Private businesses and corrupt politicians are believed to have siphoned off billions of dollars.
rationale: Corrupt politicians siphoning billions from private businesses is a loaded political-corruption claim rather than a neutral context for corrupt.
